researched_writeups.title: JD.com - by EllTec Analysis and Lukas Köppl
researched_writeups.summary: The deep dive emphasizes JD's unique 1P direct-sales model and proprietary logistics network (JD Logistics) as key moats over asset-light marketplace rivals like Alibaba and PDD in high-ticket electronics and home appliances . At $33/share ($44.6B market cap vs $23.5B EV due to ~$21B in net cash), JD trades at a forward P/E of ~9.4x while operating losses in 'New Businesses' (food delivery) narrow significantly after peaking. Catalysts include international expansion via Joybuy and the €2.2B Ceconomy acquisition, ongoing $5B share buybacks, and retail margin expansion driving over 26% EPS growth in FY2026.

researched_writeups.title: JD.com: The $39 Billion Company That's Worth $100 Billion
researched_writeups.summary: The pitch outlines a Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) valuation demonstrating that JD is severely mispriced at a $39B market cap given its $23.3B net cash position ($32.1B cash vs $8.8B debt) and majority stakes in JD Health ($16B) and JD Logistics ($6.5B). The core JD Retail business generates ~$6B in operating profit, implying that the market is pricing the core e-commerce operation at a negative or low single-digit EBIT multiple. Key operational catalysts and return drivers include capital returns via share repurchases and monetization options strategies to narrow the price-to-value gap.

researched_writeups.title: JD.com — Anyone else looking at this?
researched_writeups.summary: This detailed Reddit DD highlights JD.com as China's largest retailer by revenue ($159B) trading at a forward P/E of 7.6x, with $22B in net cash representing ~57% of its market capitalization. Stripping out net cash values the core retail business and nationwide warehousing infrastructure at roughly 3-4x earnings while free cash flow grew 66% YoY. Key catalysts include a 3.7% dividend yield, management's active $5B share buyback program, and the tapering of losses from instant retail and local delivery investments.

researched_writeups.title: Investment thesis on JD.com
researched_writeups.summary: This memo analyzes JD's first-party retail and self-operated fulfillment infrastructure as an irreplaceable brand-authenticity moat in high-value categories compared to third-party marketplaces. Applying conservative DCF and EPS valuation models on 43.7 billion RMB of free cash flow, the author shows upside potential as non-GAAP net margins expand from ~1.9% toward historical guidance of 4.0%+. Catalysts include fulfillment center cost efficiencies and sector-wide sentiment recovery in Chinese e-commerce equities.
